fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?
**Featureless mid-brown blocks. I cannot tell you what they are made of.** They are block-*shaped* — you could tell someone "blocks" — but the face carries no material. Stone, plaster, packed earth, painted board: nothing in the image chooses between them.
fields.Q1_WHY:
I measured it rather than eyeballed it. Mean absolute difference between horizontally adjacent pixels, inside a single block face, excluding joints:

| region | mean brightness | adjacent-pixel detail | max local jump |
|---|---|---|---|
| wall face, right corridor column `(450,325)-(500,340)` | 93 | **0.85** | 8 |
| wall face, right corridor column `(450,360)-(500,385)` | 127 | **1.14** | 9 |
| wall face, left corridor column `(320,360)-(372,385)` | 111 | **1.00** | 12 |
| bright band face `(445,395)-(530,418)` | 123 | 2.23 | 47 |

The brightest, closest wall face in the picture varies by about **one grey level** between neighbouring pixels, with a maximum excursion of 9 out of 127 — roughly 7%. There is no grain, no chisel mark, no chip, no pit, no colour variation within a block. What's there is a soft bilinear-looking blur with no edges in it.

There is a second problem stacked on that one. The wall faces are *smooth*; everything else in the frame is *dithered*. The blur is not a texture, it's the absence of one, and it sits directly beside crisp per-pixel work, so the walls look like they were imported from a different, lower-resolution asset set and filtered on the way in.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?
**Solid mass** — but only just, and only because of one 4-pixel line.

At `y=422–425`, across the entire width, the wall's south face drops to a flat dark bar and then the ground resumes at `y=426`. That bar is the only thing in the image asserting the wall has height. Measured at x=300 / 340 / 470: `140 → 24 → 61`, `152 → 28 → 89`, `121 → 28 → 72`. Four rows, constant value within itself, no gradient, no falloff, no visible side face, no cap. Cut those four pixels and the structure becomes a flat pattern.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?
Two transitions, and they don't match each other.

**South face of the wall run (`y=421→426`, sampled at x=470):** `121, 121, [28, 28, 28, 28], 72, 73`. **Four pixels.** One flat step down, one step back up. That's the whole event. No contact shadow, no ambient falloff, no bevel.

**Inner face of the corridor (`x=374→390` at y≈370):** `115, [39, 39], 52, 62, 71, 75, 80, 84, 86` — a 2px dark line then a **14-pixel** gradient ramp back to floor level. That's a proper occlusion falloff.

So the same wall meets the ground two different ways depending on which side you stand on: 14px of soft AO on the corridor faces, 4px of hard bar on the south face. One of those was authored and one was not.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?
**NOTHING.** I went looking hard — gamma-lifted the whole frame to 0.28 to pull content out of the dark — and found exactly two objects on 750 pixels of wall run:

1. `x 133–148, y 383–412` — a vertical post with three crossbars, sitting on the band's north edge. Reads as a ladder or a bracket. Its values are 5–20 against a background of 9–14, so at 1:1 it is **invisible**; I only found it by amplifying 9×.
2. `x 565–572, y 382–419` — a 7×38px vertical bar of a single uniform colour (24–29), overhanging the wall's top edge by 7px and stopping dead at the base line. Flat fill, no highlight, no shadow, no ends, no fixing. I cannot name what it is.

No rope, no pins, no hide, no salvaged timber, no bracing, no lintel, no keystone. For a place held by four hundred years of continuous emergency repair, there is not one repair on it.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?
**Built** — the layout is genuinely authored. Vertical joints in the band fall at x = 80, 130, 138, 156, 190, 234, 272, 286, 322, 375 … giving block widths of 50, 8, 18, 34, 44, 38, 14, 36, 53 — irregular, no stamp. Course heights in the right column are 48 / 34 / 46 — also irregular. I correlated the left corridor column against the right and against its mirror: r = −0.20 and 0.22. Not the same asset.

The bond is real. The face is empty. Someone laid out masonry and then forgot to draw any of it.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?
**YES.**

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent.** The composition, the light falloff and the corridor read are all good, and the floor is genuinely good work — but the question was about what stands here, and what stands here is the weakest thing in the frame by a distance. It is carrying nothing.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?
**Legible at 1:1:** the joint grid — the darker gaps between blocks — and the per-block value differences. The base line at y=422. That's the layout. Nothing else.

**The face itself is blank at 1:1.** Plainly: on every wall surface in this image there is no material visible without magnification.

**Only appears on magnification:** at 6–8× the faces resolve into faint soft blobs of ±4 grey levels. That's the entire payoff for zooming in, and it isn't material — it's blur.

**Change with distance from the figure:** none, in kind. The brightest wall face available — `(445,395)-(530,418)`, roughly 90px from the lamp — is just as blank as the dimmest. Distance only removes the joints: by `x<200` in the west run and `x>620` in the east run the blocks fall to values 4–50 and even the layout stops reading. So the wall goes from *blank with joints* to *blank*.
fields.Q7_WHY:
Checked at 1:1: `(445,395)-(530,418)` and `(300,395)-(375,420)` — the two brightest wall faces; `(314,255)-(376,420)` and `(439,255)-(505,420)` — both corridor columns full height; `(60,392)-(300,425)` and `(590,392)-(700,425)` — the dim west and east runs of the band.

Magnified 6–10×: the same six regions, plus `(115,370)-(165,425)` and `(545,365)-(600,420)` at 9× gamma lift to identify the two objects in Q4. Both objects are hunting, not seeing.
fields.Q8:
IS THERE ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?
Two things, and both are the same defect wearing different clothes.

**The top edge.** I scanned for it at x = 70, 110, 150, 190, 230, 270, 310, 510, 550, 590, 630, 670. It is at `y=390` at **every single one**. Not 389, not 391. A dead-straight one-pixel edge running the full width of the screen.

**The base line.** I scanned for where the `y=422–425` bar breaks. It is unbroken from `x=55` to `x=374`, and unbroken from `x=439` to `x=749` — it stops only at the corridor mouth, which is correct. That's a 320-pixel run and a 310-pixel run of perfectly constant 4-pixel line without one interruption.

The eye comes back to these because they are the only edges in the frame with no incident on them at all, and they bracket the wall top and bottom. The wall reads as extruded, not built.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?
**Nothing is drawn.** Literal black — RGB values of 1–2 — in two rectangles, `x<310` and `x>508`, from `y≈133` down to where the light cone clips them around `y≈390`. Their boundaries are dead vertical at x=310 and x=508 and dead horizontal at y=133, which are not geometry lines; that's a visibility state edge.

Above `y=133` the same regions come back at values 8–12 — remembered-but-not-visible floor. So the answer differs by where you look: north of the band it's *unseen*, at the top of the frame it's *seen-and-remembered*.

The part that matters for the structure: at `y=390` you go from value 10 to value 103 in **one pixel**. The wall has no far side, no back edge, no thickness rendered on the north face. It begins at its top edge and the void starts at exactly that pixel. Whatever is beyond, the wall itself doesn't participate in it.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?
Found it: `x 378–435`, ~57px wide, running from the band's north face at `y=421` up to `y≈65`.

**I read it as a passage.** Three things made the difference, in order of weight:

1. **Floor continuity.** The strip inside the gap is the same crisply dithered masonry the figure is standing on, and I can trace joints and a crack line through it at `y 227–290`. The walls beside it are smooth blank fill. The texture mismatch that hurts everywhere else *helps* here — passage and wall are unmistakably different surfaces.
2. **The AO ramp.** 14 pixels of contact shadow on both inner faces. Notches in a pattern don't shade themselves.
3. **Aspect ratio.** The flanking columns run parallel for ~360px. No block in the band is taller than 53px, so this cannot be read as a gap between two blocks.

One qualification, and it's real: I can tell it's a passage, but I **cannot tell it goes anywhere.** It opens into a floor area at `y≈65`, but that area sits at values 8–12 — on a phone, indistinguishable from black. At 1:1 the corridor reads as a corridor that ends in darkness at about `y=250`. Passage, yes. Destination, no.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?
**Nothing has ever happened to it.** It is pristine.

Read from: top edge at y=390 with zero deviation over 600px; base line 4px with zero deviation over two 300px+ runs; no missing blocks; no spalled corners; no filled gaps; no leaning; no settling. And the numeric proof for cracks — a crack produces a large local jump, and the maximum adjacent-pixel jump anywhere on a wall face is 8–12 grey levels out of 93–127. There isn't one.

This is the sharpest thing in the whole assessment: **the floor has cracks and the walls do not.** I can trace crack lines across the lower floor at `y≈500–690` and up the corridor at `y 227–290`. Every bit of the damage and history budget went into the ground. The thing that has been standing here in continuous heavy use since before records began, held by four centuries of orc repair, is in better condition than a new build.

---
fields.CULL: Wall faces are blank fills — no material, no damage, no repair. Only the floor was actually drawn.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Draw the wall faces at the same pixel density as the floor — the face currently varies by ~1 grey level between adjacent pixels versus ~5.6 on the floor; it needs chisel marks, pitting and per-block colour variation that survive at 1:1.
- Remove the blur. Wall surfaces are bilinear-smooth beside nearest-neighbour floor work; match the filtering so the walls stop reading as an imported asset.
- Break the two straight lines: put missing blocks, spalled corners and settling into the `y=390` top edge and the `y=422–425` base line, both of which currently run 300+ pixels without a single incident.
- Put actual repair on the wall — rope lashings, driven pins, salvaged timber across a gap — at readable contrast in the lit zone `x 280–530`, not at values 5–20 where the object at `x 133–148, y 383–412` currently sits invisible.
- Give the south face the same 14px contact-shadow ramp the corridor faces have, instead of the flat 4px bar at `y=422–425`.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context).*
